evidence: tracks.go rescanLyrics: 8 workers send to the UNBUFFERED `results` channel (line 182); the drain loop `for res := range results` (195) returns early on any SetTrackLyrics error (198). After the return nothing reads `results`, so blocked worker sends never complete, wg.Wait() never returns, and `close(results)` (192) never runs -> the workers, the wg.Wait goroutine, and (once the buffer-less `jobs` producer fills) the producer goroutine all leak permanently. HasSyncedLyrics uses r.Context() but the workers are blocked on the channel SEND, not the lyrics call, so request-context cancellation does NOT unblock them. Each failed rescan leaks up to ~9 goroutines + retained Track slice. Gated behind the admin bearer secret and requires a transient store error, which caps real-world severity at medium.
fix: Drain results to completion on error instead of returning early: on SetTrackLyrics failure record the error into a variable and `continue` ranging until the channel closes, then respond once (500 with generic msg if any error occurred). Alternatively make the worker send a `select { case results <- r: case <-r.Context().Done(): return }` AND have the drain loop still run to close. Minimal: replace the early `return` in the loop with error-capture + continue.

evidence: aibuild.go 60-93: GetLayout is read, then RemoveColumn is called for each distinct existing col (destroying the old layout; cascade FK on board_layout_cell_tracks also drops placements), UpdateBoardCols sets cols=len(cats), THEN AddColumn/PlaceTrack run in a loop that returns 500 on first error (77, 86). A failure at column 3 leaves cols 1-2 rebuilt, the rest gone, Cols possibly mismatching, with no rollback. RemoveColumn/UpdateBoardCols errors are swallowed via `_ =`. Confirmed the AdminStore interface (store.go 10-39) exposes NO transaction primitive (Begin/WithTx) and PostgresRepo runs every op on r.pool directly (admin_store.go) — so a transactional fix REQUIRES adding a store method; it cannot be done in the handler alone.
fix: Add a transactional primitive to AdminStore (e.g. `RebuildLayout(ctx, boardID string, cats []struct{Name string; Placements []Placement}) error`) implemented with pool.Begin/tx.Commit/Rollback in admin_store.go, and have aiBuild call it so clear+cols+add+place is atomic (rolls back to prior layout on any error). Also stop discarding RemoveColumn/UpdateBoardCols errors and return a generic 500 message. Cheaper interim: build the new layout in temp cols and swap, but true safety needs the tx.

evidence: layout.go attachBoard 193-204: the DB attach commits first, then LoadBoardByID; on load error the handler 500s and the engine is never reloaded -> persistent state (session.board_id set) diverges from live engine state with no rollback. That divergence half is CONFIRMED. The nil-deref half is REFUTED: the only LoadBoardByID impl (repo_postgres.go / admin_store.go 301-381) never returns (nil, nil) — an empty/non-existent board hits `if len(cells)==0 { return nil, error }` (376-378), which is handled by the error branch. So ReloadBoard is never handed a nil *game.Board via this path, and ReloadBoard itself (engine.go 256) only assigns e.board and broadcasts inside the Run loop. No panic reachable.
fix: Reorder so the engine reload is validated before/with the attach, or make attach+reload atomic: keep the load result, and only AttachBoard after LoadBoardByID succeeds (swap the two calls); if load fails, return 502/404 without having committed the attach. Optional defensive `if board == nil { 404 }` before ReloadBoard for future non-Postgres stores.

evidence: handler.go decodeJSON (120-123) wraps r.Body in json.NewDecoder with no http.MaxBytesReader and no limit. Every mutating handler (createBoard, renameBoard, addTrack, addColumn, renameCategory, setTrackOverride, attachBoard, placeTrack) decodes before any field-length validation, and those length checks (name<=200, artist/song<=200, category<=100) run only AFTER a full Decode. A large JSON string in a known field, or deep nesting, forces unbounded allocation. Streaming does not save it — a single giant scalar value is buffered. Confirmed reachable, but every route is behind the admin bearer secret (middleware.go), so it is an authenticated memory-DoS -> medium.
fix: In decodeJSON take the ResponseWriter (or wrap at the mux/CORS layer): `r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)` before `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(v)`. Optionally add dec.DisallowUnknownFields(). Signature change ripples to all callers but is mechanical.

evidence: handler.go CORSHandler (99-110) does set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all responses — factually confirmed. But the finding's own scenario is self-correcting and the headline 'any web origin can call/read the admin API' is misleading: auth is a Bearer header (middleware.go), Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is NOT set, so a cross-origin page cannot attach the Authorization header the auth middleware requires and cannot read authenticated responses without already possessing the secret. Residual risk is near-zero (origin-agnostic probing only). Real vulnerability is low/hardening, not a live exposure.
fix: Reflect an allow-list of first-party origins (stage/mobile/admin) instead of '*'; never pair '*' with Allow-Credentials. If '*' is intentional for a header-token API, leave it and document the rationale — no code change strictly required for security.

evidence: Every handler returns raw err.Error() in 500s: boards.go (13,37,47,57,86,95), layout.go (12,43,57,61,78,91,95,123,151,172,200), tracks.go (17,27,81,127,144,161,198), aibuild.go (31,77,86). Store errors are wrapped as `store: ...: %w` (admin_store.go) carrying the underlying pgx text (table/column/constraint names). That text reaches the client verbatim. Gated behind the admin secret, so schema disclosure is to an already-authenticated caller -> low.
fix: Add a small helper e.g. `serverError(w, err)` that logs the real error server-side and writes http.Error(w, "internal error", 500); replace the ~25 `http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500)` sites with it. Mechanical, no behavior change beyond the client message.

evidence: layout.go placeTrack (129-155): col bounded only 1-8 (not board.Cols), body.Pos taken raw from JSON, decode error discarded (147). The 'phantom-column placement corrupts layout' claim is REFUTED by the schema: board_layout_cell_tracks has FOREIGN KEY (board_id,row,col) REFERENCES board_layout_cells(board_id,row,col) (0002_boards.sql). AddColumn only creates cells for real columns, so PlaceTrack into a non-existent col fails the FK -> PostgresRepo.PlaceTrack returns an error -> 500 (leaked, cf adminapi-6). No corrupt phantom row is written. CONFIRMED remainder: `pos` (INT NOT NULL, no CHECK in schema) accepts negative/huge values from body.Pos, and the decode error is silently ignored — a low-impact ordering/robustness gap.
fix: Validate pos into a sane range (e.g. 0..4) and stop discarding the decodeJSON error (return 400 on malformed body). Bounding col to board.Cols is optional defense-in-depth (a nicer 409 than the current FK-driven 500) — fetch the board like addColumn does and reject col > board.Cols.

evidence: layout.go renameCategory (102-127) checks only body.Category != "" (117) — no length cap, unlike addColumn which enforces len<=100 (36-39). RenameCategory (admin_store.go 192-200) UPDATEs the TEXT category column (schema: category TEXT, unbounded). So PATCH /api/boards/{id}/columns/{col} persists an arbitrarily large category string. Combined with the missing body-size limit (adminapi-4) this allows storage/payload bloat. Auth-gated -> low.
fix: Add `if len(body.Category) > 100 { http.Error(w, "category too long (max 100)", 400); return }` after the empty check, matching addColumn.

evidence: REPRO: /tmp probe built a request to '...:generateContent?key=AIzaSyREAL_SECRET_KEY_12345' against a refused host and wrapped the transport error as fmt.Errorf("ai: request: %w", err) exactly like gemini.go 119. Output: `ai: request: Post "https://.../generateContent?key=AIzaSyREAL_SECRET_KEY_12345": dial tcp ...: connect: connection refused`, KEY_LEAKED: true. Go's *url.Error.Error() does NOT redact query params (only userinfo password), so the key survives. aibuild.go 47-50 writes that err.Error() straight to the client via http.Error(..., 502). GEMINI_API_KEY is therefore disclosed in the response body (and any logs) on any transport failure. Reachable only with the admin bearer secret, and the AI feature must be wired, so real severity medium rather than high — but it discloses a distinct credential to whoever holds admin access and into proxy/access logs.
fix: aibuild.go: log the real error server-side and return a fixed message: `http.Error(w, "AI build failed", http.StatusBadGateway)`. Combine with ai-2 (move key to a header) so it never sits in the URL at all.

evidence: gemini.go 110: `url := apiBase + c.model + ":generateContent?key=" + c.apiKey` — the key is a query param. Confirmed this is what makes ai-1 leak (the probe reproduced the key surviving in *url.Error). Query-string secrets are also captured by proxies/access logs/traces. Header delivery keeps it out of URL-based logging entirely.
fix: gemini.go: `url := apiBase + c.model + ":generateContent"` and `req.Header.Set("x-goog-api-key", c.apiKey)` after building the request. Google's generativelanguage API accepts the key via the x-goog-api-key header.

evidence: gemini.go 122: `raw, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)` — no io.LimitReader, no size cap; the read error is discarded (surfaces later as a decode failure). The http.Client Timeout of 60s (line 42) bounds time but not bytes, so a multi-GB streamed response is fully buffered in memory. CONFIRMED as written. Real severity is low, not medium: the peer is Gemini over TLS (generativelanguage.googleapis.com), so exploitation requires a compromised Google endpoint or a TLS MITM — not a realistic on-path attacker for an outbound HTTPS call.
fix: gemini.go: `raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` and check err (return fmt.Errorf("ai: read response: %w", err)). 1MB dwarfs any legitimate categories JSON.

evidence: gemini.go buildPrompt 167: `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s — %s — %s\n", t.ID, t.Artist, t.Song)` interpolates artist/song (attacker-influenceable via imported playlist titles) into the prompt with no delimiting/escaping — classic prompt injection. Track-ID and placement impact IS neutralized: aibuild.go guards with byID[tid] (82), placed[tid], and row>rows, so hallucinated/duplicate IDs and over-fill are dropped. Residual (confirmed) risk = the model can be steered to emit arbitrary category NAMES. Critically, aiBuild calls h.store.AddColumn directly (76) which does NOT length- or content-cap the name (only the addColumn HTTP handler caps at 100), so attacker-chosen category text is stored uncapped and later rendered on the stage board. Whether that becomes XSS depends on the (unreviewed) stage frontend's rendering; content/derailment injection is confirmed regardless.
fix: In buildPrompt, emit the track list as a JSON data block (json.Marshal the []TrackInput) or quote+escape artist/song, and instruct the model to treat it as data. In aiBuild, sanitize/cap cat.Name (e.g. len<=100, strip control chars) before AddColumn. Ensure the stage renders category names as text, not HTML.

evidence: Duplicate of adminapi-2 at aibuild.go 60-93. Confirmed: non-atomic clear-then-rebuild, old layout wiped before new one committed, mid-loop 500 leaves a half-built board, RemoveColumn/UpdateBoardCols errors swallowed, and the 500 body leaks the raw store error (ai-1/adminapi-6 class). Confirmed no transaction primitive exists on AdminStore (store.go 10-39); PostgresRepo uses r.pool per-op, so the fix requires adding a tx-backed store method — same conclusion as adminapi-2.
fix: Same as adminapi-2: add a tx-backed RebuildLayout method to AdminStore/PostgresRepo (pool.Begin + Commit/Rollback) and call it from aiBuild so clear+cols+add+place is atomic; return a generic 500 message.

evidence: aibuild.go 74-92: the over-fill/hallucination/dup guards (row>rows, !byID[tid], placed[tid]) are correct and prevent any crash or nil-deref at game time (LoadBoardByID/newGridFromCells fill nil cells with empty game.Cell, repo_postgres.go 237-243). Under-fill (fewer than cols categories, or sparse columns) is real but the finding itself labels it 'acceptable-by-design per the admin-tweaks-after note' and 'not a crash'. This is confirmed intended behavior, not a defect — refuted as a bug. Purely informational / optional UX polish.
fix: Optional only: after the apply loop, if placed < rows*len(cats) or len(cats) < cols, include a warning/hint in the JSON response so the admin knows the board is sparse. No correctness fix needed.
